selection_note: Thirteenth source-disjoint five-assessment screening cohort selected from the current included Index S1=A, S2=C records. All 60 sources in the preceding 12 merged manifests are excluded case-insensitively; no additional open Upstream assessment-batch PR was visible at selection. Prioritize source-specific S2 interference mechanisms and feasible offline first-party Python/Node tests; these are questions, not known bugs. Current public source heads and licenses were inspected. Screening is serial; no live models, provider calls, browser episodes, external fork/PR publication, Index regrade or autonomy claim.

candidates.finding: The assessed S2=C witness groups specialist jobs and rejects concurrent use of one connector. Check whether team-group admission and parent-chat uniqueness remain sound under competing starts or partial group-launch failure, using genuine first-party Python functions and fixed state without starting any model worker.
candidates.screening_result: A synthetic simultaneous direct call to start_team bypassing the HTTP entry can double-register a team, but the real first-party ThreadingHTTPServer.do_POST holds the same shared RLock around every store.action('team-start'). The supposed race cannot be reproduced through the supported native entry without removing that guard. No credible product defect or useful patch has been established; experimental direct-call-only patch and test were discarded. MIT license; lexical public team-concurrency issue/PR search found no matching report. No agent/provider ran.

candidates.finding: The assessed S2=C witness serializes and verifies shared session-memory updates. Screen current first-party memory.py plus test_memory_concurrency.py for a falsifiable lost-update or stale-write failure between separate sessions, with isolated files and no agent or provider invocation.
candidates.observed_native_change: Two genuine MemoryStore mutator-vs-append interleavings FAIL on untouched first-party 7b2f57b (lost accepted note); after the bounded reentrant-lock fix, 7/7 native tests PASS including the five original memory concurrency tests. A disposable clean pinned source replay of the exact archived patch passes git apply --check, the seven tests and git diff --check.

candidates.finding: The assessed S2=C mechanism prevents two independently operating Actors from owning the same shared resource. Test the current first-party claims.ts admission/release path for conflicting versus disjoint resource claims and stale-owner handling with native isolated fixtures, without launching model agents.
candidates.blocker: Current MIT first-party claim/release path is synchronous and SQLite-backed; no source-supported concurrent wrong-owner native failure is established inside the documented single-Hub boundary. The obvious cross-process read-then-replace concern is not yet shown as a supported mode. Node 24 is present, but npm run build fails because tsc/dependencies are unavailable; no genuine first-party native regression could be run. Need a supported interleaving or multi-server contract plus dependency-enabled native test before proposing a code change. Public overlap search found the original claims feature PR #41, not an independently verified defect. No agent/provider or external write.

candidates.finding: The assessed S2=C witness uses a worker mesh and queue/pump to attenuate worker-node overcommit across Executor jobs. Inspect the first-party mesh, scheduling and release paths for inconsistent capacity admission or failure recovery under fixed offline Node fixtures, not live agent/provider execution.
candidates.screening_result: Current MIT source e705e872 supports explicit least-loaded capacity, ticket-sticky assignment, release and offline/unregister handling. Eight direct Node 24 assertions on the genuine first-party WorkerMeshRegistry all PASS (capacity refusal, ticket reuse, release, offline and node removal); the source-integrated runtime releases after transaction commit and existing native tests explicitly cover assignment failures and queue skips. No independently falsified native behavior or need for a patch was established. Vitest's broader scripted-model episodes were deliberately not run; no live agent/provider or external write.

candidates.finding: The assessed S2=C constructor detects cross-run file overlap and routes affected plan commitments into an approval-gated adjustment. Test whether current first-party overlap analysis misclassifies create/delete or path alias changes and whether the unchanged plan is preserved when adjustment is withheld, using native deterministic fixtures only.
candidates.observed_native_change: Two pure genuine first-party domain assertions FAIL on untouched source 1eeff6b: equivalent repo-relative plan paths are falsely disjoint and a landed modification is falsely unaffected. After POSIX lexical path normalization, 8 direct native Node 24 assertions PASS, including two regressions and six controls. Detached clean pinned replay passes git apply --check, apply, eight assertions and git diff --check. First-party Vitest dependencies are absent; its added tests were not run via Vitest.
candidates.limit: Lexical path normalization does not resolve symlinks or absolute-root aliases. Interactive approval-withheld adjustment behavior was inspected but not empirically exercised, because no model or interactive session was authorized.
